abstract: Motivation Most omics data is stored by compressors that treat it as an unstructured byte stream. Format-aware compressors close that gap but are fragmented across formats and often expect a training pass over the user's own file. A general-purpose lossless compressor that is applicable to the most storage-intense omics data formats while beating the general codecs on ratio and speed would offer significant savings for large omics datasets storage and data retrieval. Results We present NYX, a compressor for FASTA, FASTQ, BED and VCF files. It leverages a reversible, format-specific transform optimised for the OpenZL compression algorithm to reach compression ratios up to 2.3 times those of the strongest general-purpose codecs (zstd -19, xz -9e and 7-Zip) while compressing up to two orders of magnitude faster. On the 1000 Genomes VCF dataset NYX reaches a compression ratio of 468.67x, 2.0 times that of xz -9e while compressing 1.8 times faster. On mammalian FASTA assemblies totalling 9.3 GB, NYX is within 3-4% of NAF, the strongest purpose-built FASTA codec, while compressing 57-73 times faster. Across all 54 inputs no single codec beats NYX on ratio and compression speed together: the tools that achieve higher compression are 1.2 to 73 times slower. NYX provides fully lossless, fast and efficient compression under one easy-to-use tool for the most common omics data types. Availability and implementation Source code, the shipped models, the benchmark harness and the scripts that regenerate every figure and table: https://github.com/Georgakopoulos-Soares-lab/compression
